text:
Nikhil Sharma: sharing the latest onboarding flow AC + edge cases for purchase -> entitlement -> org linking. want to lock today so Eng/QA can test consistently. doc is in the design spec section (same one from last week) but pasting the contentious bits here.

Nikhil Sharma: Proposed acceptance criteria (AWS first, mirror for GCP):
1) If customer has a valid marketplace entitlement, Console shows “Marketplace purchase detected” + prompts to link to a Redwood org.
2) Org linking requires Org Admin role.
3) After linking, entitlements activate within 5 min (p95) and user sees “Active” state + what SKU/add-ons are enabled.
4) If entitlement hasn’t arrived yet, show “Pending purchase verification” state w/ guidance + auto-refresh.
5) If multiple entitlements exist (multiple AWS accounts / multiple subscriptions), user can select which entitlement to link.
6) If entitlement maps to a different Redwood org already, show “Already linked” + support CTA (no silent reassignment).

Nikhil Sharma: Edge cases we need to decide language/behavior on:
- buyer purchased in AWS account A but signs in w/ AWS account B / different identity provider
- “delayed entitlement” from AWS (we’ve seen >30 min in some partner sandbox cases)
- user links wrong Redwood org (we’ve had tickets on this)
- region mismatch (purchased in us-east-1 but trying to provision eu-west)

Lauren Bishop: +1 on requiring Org Admin. For wrong org: do we allow self-serve unlink/relink or force support? Support load vs risk.

Ethan Park: on delayed entitlement: we should assume webhook/eventual consistency, not guarantee 5 min for all. We can do 5 min target but UX should be resilient up to ~60 min without looking broken.

Ethan Park: technical note: on AWS, we’ll get entitlement via AWS MP events + ResolveCustomer callback. sometimes ResolveCustomer is immediate but entitlements list is empty for a bit. we can:
- store “purchase token” once we see ResolveCustomer
- poll entitlements every N minutes until populated
- surface “pending” with last checked time

Chloe Martin: for Console UX, we should separate:
A) “We identified your marketplace purchase” (based on ResolveCustomer/purchase token)
B) “Your entitlement is active” (based on entitlement ingestion)

Chloe Martin: otherwise users think linking failed when it’s really AWS lag. we can show stepper:
1. Verify purchase (done)
2. Link org (user)
3. Activate entitlements (pending/active)

Naomi Feldman: pls be careful on wording in #3 ("activate within 5 min"). for security/compliance reviews we can’t promise a strict timeline unless we can meet it. recommend: “typically within a few minutes; may take up to X; contact support if >Y”.

Leila Farouk: from QA POV, we need deterministic states for E2E.
- if webhook is delayed, we need a way in staging to simulate pending state + then flip to active
- add an explicit “Refresh status” button so tests don’t rely only on timers

Nikhil Sharma: makes sense. what’s our max “up to X” that’s still sane? i’ve personally seen AWS MP take ~20-30 min for entitlement to show.

Dev Patel: support angle: if we let self-serve unlink/relink, we need guardrails + audit trail. most painful tickets are “i linked to wrong org” and “entitlement never activated”.

Dev Patel: suggestion:
- allow unlink ONLY if entitlement is not yet Active (still Pending)
- once Active, require support to move entitlement (to avoid abuse + accidental disruptions)
- always show entitlement id + AWS account id (last 4) so support can verify quickly

Lauren Bishop: +1. Dedicated/Private SKUs also have higher risk if people can bounce entitlements around.

Ethan Park: re: multiple AWS accounts / multiple subscriptions
- a single user might have access to multiple AWS payer accounts; we’ll see multiple entitlements.
- we should display a picker: “Choose the subscription to link” with identifiers:
  - Product/SKU name
  - Entitlement ID
  - AWS account (masked)
  - Status (active/expired)

Ethan Park: also, idempotency: linking should be safe to click multiple times; backend should treat as upsert keyed by (provider, entitlement_id).

Chloe Martin: UX question: if user logs into Redwood and we don’t see purchase token (no ResolveCustomer) but they *did* purchase, what do we do?

Nikhil Sharma: currently the proposal is: Console onboarding wizard has “I purchased via AWS Marketplace” path where they paste “Marketplace customer identifier” / “Entitlement ID” (or follow a deep link from AWS). but not sure if AWS gives an easy copy/paste id.

Ethan Park: AWS gives a “customer identifier” on the redirect (ResolveCustomer) path. If they don’t come through the redirect, we can’t reliably map without them re-opening the product from Marketplace.

Elliot Price: docs can cover that explicitly:
- “After purchase, launch Redwood Inference from AWS Marketplace to complete org linking.”
- troubleshooting: “If you signed up directly first, you must still return to Marketplace and click ‘Set up your account’ to generate the link.”

Naomi Feldman: +1, and we should avoid asking them to paste opaque IDs unless we’re sure it’s available and not sensitive. Better to instruct “re-launch from marketplace”.

Leila Farouk: we should add AC for that:
- If no purchase token exists, Console should show “We can’t find a marketplace purchase for this account yet” + button “Open AWS Marketplace instructions” (link to docs) instead of dead-ending.

Nikhil Sharma: ok. region mismatch: do we block linking if entitlement is tied to a region?

Ethan Park: entitlement itself isn’t region-scoped the same way, but our provisioning might be. We should link org regardless, then show “choose region” and if unsupported, show clear error + recommended regions.

Lauren Bishop: for Private/VPC, region is a big deal. but agreed: linking should be independent. provisioning UI should enforce region constraints.

Chloe Martin: so AC tweak:
- Linking step never asks for region.
- After activation, Console shows eligible regions based on SKU + org policy.

Dev Patel: +1. For support, the biggest win is specific errors. “Region mismatch” should say:
“Your subscription is active, but your org is not enabled in eu-west-1. Switch region to us-east-1 or contact support to request enablement.”

Nikhil Sharma: summarizing proposed decisions:
- Update AC #3 wording: “typically a few minutes; may take up to 60 minutes. if >60, contact support.”
- Add explicit stepper states (verify purchase / link org / activate entitlements).
- Add “Refresh status” button.
- Unlink policy: self-serve unlink only while Pending; once Active, support-only.
- Multiple entitlements: show picker with masked AWS account + entitlement id.
- If no purchase token, direct user back to Marketplace launch flow (docs).

Naomi Feldman: works for me. pls ensure we have audit logging for: link/unlink attempts + which admin did it.

Ethan Park: we already planned audit events for link/unlink + entitlement activation. will confirm schema w/ Marcus but should be straightforward.

Leila Farouk: for QA, can we add a staging-only admin endpoint/flag to force entitlement state transitions? otherwise tests will be flaky.

Ethan Park: yes, we can add a test fixture to ingestion pipeline (similar to how we do billing meters). I’ll sync w/ Leila on exact needs.

Chloe Martin: I’ll update the Console copy to reflect the “up to 60 min” language + add the “Refresh” CTA. will share strings in DES-213.

Elliot Price: I’ll make sure docs page includes: “launch from marketplace” requirement + screenshots of Pending vs Active. also add “what info to send support” section (org id, entitlement id, AWS account last 4).

Nikhil Sharma: perfect. I’ll update the AC doc with these changes + tag Eng/Support. :thumbsup:

(reactions: Lauren Bishop :+1:; Ethan Park :white_check_mark:; Dev Patel :+1:; Naomi Feldman :eyes:)
